segmenti.tekst: إن الحمد لله نحمده ونستعينه ونستغفره

ونعوذ بالله من شرور أنفسنا ومن سيئات أعمالنا، من يهده الله فلا مضل له ومن يضلل فلا هادي له، وأشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا عبده ورسوله، أرسله الله بالحق بشيرا ونذيرا وسراجا منيرا، لينذر من كان حيا ويحق القول على الكافرين، صلى الله تعالى عليه وعلى آله الطيبين الطاهرين وأصحابه الكرام الهداة المهتدين وسلم تسليما كثيرا إلى يوم الدين.
قال الله في كتابه الكريم: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. أما بعد.

…upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him). Dear brothers, respected members of the congregation, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, revealed this Qur'an to us through the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, so that it would be a signpost for people, guidance, light, so that its verses would guide to what is good

and turn away from what is bad, so that its verses would be of benefit to people both in this world and in the world to come. Among such verses are the verses, the last verses of Surah Al-An'am, in which Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, recommends ten things, ten commandments. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says at the beginning of these verses, addressing

Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, and then also his ummah, his followers: "Qul" – say, say, O Muhammad, O Messenger of Allah – "ta'alaw atlu ma harrama Rabbukum 'alaykum" – come, let me tell you what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, enjoins upon you, what He forbids you. What is the first thing Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, commands us, enjoins upon us? Of course, dear brothers, it is the worship of Him alone, of Him alone.
That you do not ascribe partners to Him in worship. That you do not regard others as equal to Him. That you prostrate only to Him.
That you slaughter your sacrifice (qurban) only in His name. That you swear only by Him. The Messenger of Allah, Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, was asked…

What does Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say? "That you ascribe, or regard someone else as equal to Allah, when He created you." He gave you everything, and after all that a person prays to someone else, to some dead person, to some shrine (turbe), to some saint (wali), regards some human being as a deity who can do everything, and so on, and so on.

And then he falls, falls into polytheism, into shirk. May Allah protect us. The second thing, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "wa bil-walidayni ihsana" – and that you do good to your parents, that you show kindness to your parents.
See, dear brothers, how Islam, or how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, immediately after the command to worship Him alone commands kindness to parents.
How important is kindness to parents? On one occasion the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, said: "He is ruined, he is ruined, he is ruined." And they asked him: "Who, O Messenger of Allah?"

He says: "The one who lives to see both his parents or one of them reach old age, and that does not get him into Jannah (Paradise)" – kindness to his parents does not get him into Jannah. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in another verse: "وَقَضَى رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعْبُدُوا إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ" – and Allah commands you, your Lord commands you not to worship anyone but Him – "وَبِالْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَانًا" – and to behave well towards your parents – "فَلَا تَقُلْ لَهُمَا أُفٍّ" – and you may not even say "uff" to them.

Also, in the time of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, a man came and asked him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, who has the most right to my company, to my kind word, to my presence?"

What does Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, say to him? "Your mother." Then after that, he says: "Your mother." Then after that: "Your mother." And after that, he says: "O Messenger of Allah…", he says: "Your father." Ibn Abbas, radiyallahu ta'ala anhu (may Allah be pleased with him): "Man lam yaqum bi haqqil-walidayni lam yaqum bi haqqillah." He says: whoever does not respect, or does not fulfil, the right of his parents will not fulfil the right, the right of Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, either. The third thing, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says:
"وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا أَوْلَادَكُمْ مِنْ إِمْلَاقٍ نَحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ" – and He says: do not kill your children out of fear of poverty. We provide for you, and for them as well.
You know that the Arabs before, in that pre-Islamic era, killed their children, buried their baby girls alive. But today too, dear brothers, we have a high rate of abortion.

A high rate of abortion. We see that a man has three children and, thinking that the fourth one his wife is carrying will bring poverty, he agrees together with his wife, and she aborts that child; they kill that child.

What does the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, tell us? He says: after 120 days Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, sends an angel and commands him to breathe the soul into the child while it is still in the womb. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, also commands that its provision (rizq) be written for it, provision and wealth, sustenance, that its death be written, that what it will do in the course of its life be written, and whether it will be among the people of Jannah or Jahannam (Hellfire).

That is why, dear brothers, many children are not a cause of poverty, but a cause of Allah's blessing, a cause of wealth. The Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "I will boast," he says, "of you on the Day of Judgement, of how numerous you are."

So it is praiseworthy and good for a person, a Muslim, to have as many children as possible and by no means to fear for provision, because the One who gives you provision will give it to him too, will give him too wealth and sustenance. The fourth thing, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says:

and He says: do not approach those vile, ugly deeds, whether open or secret. There are deeds, ugly, vile ones, that are expressed with the tongue: cursing, backbiting, scheming. And there are also those that a person does with his actions, such as zina (fornication),

such as – a person going to places where a Muslim is not permitted to go, and so on, everything that is obviously ugly. And, dear brothers, [unclear] Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says, and He says: do not approach. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, does not say "do not do" – "do not approach". Today we have people who are, masha Allah, ready to go into the town centre, and to places where there are scantily dressed girls, where there is alcohol,

where there is hookah and so on, where women of low morals go, and he says: "That doesn't affect me, I'm strong." It's not about whether you're strong; it is haram for you. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: do not approach. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: "wa la taqtulun-nafsal-lati harramallahu illa bil-haqq" – and He says: do not kill, do not kill the soul, the person, whom Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, has forbidden you to kill,
except in the case of exacting justice, when someone kills someone. But that is not up to us; we are not a Sharia state and so on.

That is why, dear brothers, every soul is fundamentally innocent and a person must not attack another person. And you will see that people kill each other – why? Over a parking spot. A man kills a man over a parking spot or over traffic.

This one honked at him, that one got out, and then they kill each other. One ends up in the grave, the other in prison. Both of their lives destroyed. Not only theirs, but also their families'. So it is…

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, at the end of the verse… Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, enjoins this so that, so that, He says, [unclear], so that you would reflect. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: "وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُ" – and He says: do not approach the wealth of the orphan until he comes of age, except in the best way. And, unfortunately, you have,

we have such cases: a brother passes away, a father passes away, the paternal uncle remains. What does the uncle do? The uncle takes all the property and leaves nothing to those children, those orphans. What does Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, say: "Innal-ladhina ya'kuluna amwalal-yatama zulman innama ya'kuluna fi butunihim nara" – those who, He says, unjustly consume

the wealth of orphans, He says, Allah will make them eat fire on the Day of Judgement that will devour their stomachs, their intestines, their insides. That is the punishment for those who unjustly consume the wealth of orphans.

Unless a person takes that wealth and invests it in something that will be useful for that orphan. Such as buying some land, and then after a few years the price of that land rises. Everything is for the benefit of that orphan. Or in any other way… or else a person is unjustly consuming, unjustly consuming the wealth of orphans.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says, and He says: when you measure with a measure, on a scale, measure justly. He warns, dear brothers, those who have shops, who have markets, to measure justly. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Waylun lil-mutaffifin" – He says: woe to the mutaffifin. Who are the mutaffifin? "Alladhina idhaktalu 'alan-nasi yastawfun" – those who, when something is measured for them, demand to be given the full scale, the full measure, so that no one short-changes them,
"wa idha kaluhum aw wazanuhum yukhsirun" – but when they measure for others, they short-change them. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: woe, woe to those who short-change others in measuring.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, further says: [unclear – verse in Arabic], Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says. And He says: when you speak – be just. You are reconciling your brother and your neighbour,

and the neighbour is in the right – it is on you to tell the truth, to be just. It does not matter that this is your own brother. Or if you are reconciling your sister with her husband, if they are quarrelling, and he is in the right, you should stand by him, even though she is your sister. A person should be just when he speaks, when he is a witness in court. Today there is false testimony.
There is a lot of false testimony. People, in someone's favour or because of something… people, people bear false witness. So a person should fear these things.

He further says, the ninth thing, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Wa bi 'ahdillahi awfu" – and fulfil, He says, Allah's… what you have vowed to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. There are people who say: "I vow to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, that I will pray all my prayers in the mosque."

You must fulfil it. "I vow that I will not cheat." No cheating then. "I vow this and that." You must fulfil it to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala. "I vow that I will not commit such-and-such a sin." Then you must not commit it. You must carry out that promise to Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala.

You must fulfil the vow. And the last thing, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "وَأَنَّ هَذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيمًا فَاتَّبِعُوهُ" – and, He says, this is My straight path, so follow it. This is the last commandment in this surah.

He says: what I have enumerated, this is the straight path. So follow this straight path. See, dear brothers, how Islam calls to everything that is good. Go back to these, and you will see how everything that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, calls to is beneficial for the individual, for a community.

And He says: do not follow other paths, lest they divert you from Allah's, lest they divert you from Allah's path. You will see today: there are people who have made everything halal, permitted everything – both sheikhs, and effendis, and muftis, and so on.

A person should return to the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. There are those who invent various innovations (bid'ah) in the religion, insert them. Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam…

Did his companions do that? [unclear] he starts nodding his head, doesn't know what to answer, doesn't know how to behave. And that is why, dear brothers, a person must not follow the passions of others, nor his own, but should follow Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, and His Messenger.

And these are the ten, ten things that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, enjoins upon us, in which there is benefit both for the person, for the individual, and for the whole, for the whole community. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who fulfil their obligations towards Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among those who worship Him alone. I ask Him, the Exalted, to gather us together in Jannah. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. Aqulu qawli hadha wa astaghfirullaha li wa lakum, fastaghfiruhu, innahu huwal-Ghafurur-Rahim.
